title_ar: فضيلة الشيخ يصدر بيانا حول حادثة إحراق بعض كتب الفقه المالكي بنوكشوط
title_en: The Sheikh Issues a Statement on the Incident of the Burning of Some Books of Maliki Jurisprudence in Nouakchott
body_ar: أصدر فضيلة الشيخ العلامة محمد الحسن ولد الددو أول أمس الجمعة 05 جمادى الثانية 1433هـ الموافق: 27 إبريل 2012 بيانا هاما حول حرق بعض تراث المالكية بنواكشوط، مدينا هذه الفعلة الشنعاء، ومعتبرا أنها "منتهى الجهالة والسفه" وتصرفا طائشا قد يكون مقدمة لإحراق جميع كتب الفقه والسنة المطهرة وحتى المصحف الشريف. واستغرب فضيلة الشيخ في البيان صدور هذا الفعل ممن يدعي الثقافة، مضيفا أنه كان الأولى به تحديد قضيته والاشتغال بخدمتها وتحديد عدوه والاشتغال بما يضره، بدل إحراق كتب خارجة عن سياق القضية جملة وتفصيلا، وذلك ما لا يشتغل به عاقل فضلا عن مسلم، وأكد فضيلة الشيخ أن هذه الكتب المحروقة ليست إنتاجا محليا ولا علاقة لها بقضية الرق في موريتانيا. وتعرض الشيخ في بيانه لتفريق العلماء في كتب الفقه بين الأحكام الشرعية المتعلقة بكل من الأحرار والعبيد، معتمدين في ذلك على ما جاء في القرآن الكريم والسنة المطهرة المتواترة، ولا يحل لمؤمن إنكاره، فقد أجمع المسلمون على أصل التفريق وعلى وجوده في العديد من أبواب الأحكام الشرعية، وأورد فضيلته خلاف العلماء في وجوب الجمعة على العبيد، ذاكرا أن مرد خلافهم إنما هو لتعارض الأدلة في هذه المسألة، ولا علاقة له بالخلاف المنعدم في أصلها. وكشف فضيلة الشيخ في بيانه عن أن هذه المسائل الفقهية المتعلقة بالعبيد والأحرار إنما يحتاج عند تحقق العبودية ووجودها بالفعل، وهو ما لا ينطبق على سياق الواقع في موريتانيا اليوم. وأفتى فضيلة الشيخ في نهاية البيان بوجوب تبيين خطر هذه الحادثة، باعتبارها منكرا بشعا يجب إنكاره على كل من سمع به من المسلمين، داعيا الله تعالى أن يصلح أحوال المسلمين وأن يهديهم صراطه المستقيم.. وهذا نص البيان: بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم وصلى الله على نبيه الكريم الحمد لله على كل حال.. أما بعد فإن مما يندى له الجبين ويمتلئ له القلب حزنا وحسرة ما تناقلته اليوم وسائل الإعلام من إقدام المسمى برام بن الداه على تمزيق كتب الدين الإسلامي وتحريقها في بلاد المسلمين وبمحضر المسلمين لا لسبب إلا لدعواه أنها تكرس العبودية، وهذا لعمري منتهى الجهالة والسفه، حيث زعم أنه تبين له أن كتب الفقه المالكي ترسخ التمييز في الأحكام بين الأحرار والعبيد، كأن ذلك مختص بالفقه المالكي، ومقتضى هذا التصرف الطائش أن يحرق القرآن أيضا وجميع كتب السنة والفقه فكلها كذلك، وكان الأولى بمن يَدَّعي الثقافة وتُدَّعى له أن يحدد قضيته ويشتغل بما يخدمها وأن يحدد عدوه ويشتغل بما يضره، أما إحراق كتب الدين التي هي خارجة عن سياق القضية جملة وتفصيلا فلا يشتغل به عاقل فضلا عن مسلم، فإن هذه الكتب التي أحرق نسخة واحدة من كل منها لكل واحد منها ملايين النسخ في العالم فلا ينقص أعدادها وانتشارها إحراقه هو لنسخة واحدة منها، وليس واحد منها إنتاجا محليا ولا علاقة لواحد منها بقضية الرق في موريتانيا، وإن كانت هذه الكتب قد تعرضت للتفريق في الأحكام الشرعية بين الأحرار والعبيد فقد فرق الله بينهما في كتابه ورسوله صلى الله عليه وسلم في سنته المتواترة عنه، ولا يستطيع من يؤمن بالله واليوم الآخر إنكار ذلك، وقد أجمع المسلمون على أصل هذا التفريق وعلى وجوده في أبواب كثيرة من الأحكام، وإن اختلفوا في بعض الأحكام فليس ذلك راجعا إلى الاختلاف في أصل المسألة، وإنما هو راجع إلى تعارض الأدلة، كالخلاف بينهم في التفريق بين الحر والعبد في أحكام الجمعة فقد ذهب جمهور المسلمين ومنهم المذاهب الأربعة إلى هذا التفريق اعتمادا على حديث طارق بن شهاب أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: «الجمعة حق واجب على كل مسلم في جماعة إلا أربعة: عبد مملوك أو امرأة أو صبي أو مريض» رواه أبو داوود عن طارق مرسلا، ورواه الحاكم عن طارق عن أبي موسى الأشعري موصولا مرفوعا، وقال الحافظ: وصححه غير واحد، وذهب الظاهرية إلى عدم التفريق بين الحر والعبد في أحكام الجمعة لأنهم رأوا أن هذا الحديث لا يقوى على تخصيص عموم القرآن، لكن هذه المسائل الفقهية إنما يحتاج إليها عند وجود العبودية وتحققها، وهو أمر خارج عن سياق الواقع في موريتانيا اليوم. لهذا رأيت من الواجب علي أن أبين خطر هذا الأمر وبشاعة هذا المنكر الذي أقدم عليه برام ووجوب إنكاره على كل من سمع به من المسلمين فلو كان أحرق نقودا أو مالا آخر غير الفقه لكان ذلك منكرا فكيف بهذه الكتب المتضمنة لشرع الله، نسأل الله أن يصلح أحوال المسلمين وأن يهديهم إلى صراطه المستقيم. كتبه محمد الحسن ولد الددو بتاريخ 1433/06/05هـ الموافق: 2012/04/27م لتحميل البيان اضغط هنا:
body_en:
*[This record has two authors. What follows down to "And this is the text of the statement" is the site's news summary. Everything after that is the Sheikh's own signed statement, reproduced in full.]*

*[Site news summary]* The day before yesterday, Friday 5 Jumada al-Thaniyah 1433 AH, corresponding to 27 April 2012, the eminent scholar Sheikh Muhammad al-Hasan Ould al-Dedew issued an important statement concerning the burning of part of the Maliki heritage in Nouakchott, condemning this hideous deed, holding it to be "the utmost ignorance and folly" and a reckless act that may be a prelude to the burning of all the books of jurisprudence and of the purified sunnah, and even of the noble Qur'anic codex.

In the statement the Sheikh expressed astonishment that such an act should issue from one who lays claim to culture, adding that it would have been more fitting for him to identify his cause and busy himself with serving it, and to identify his enemy and busy himself with what harms that enemy, rather than burning books which lie outside the context of the cause in whole and in detail — something no person of sound mind would busy himself with, let alone a Muslim. The Sheikh affirmed that these burned books are not a local product and have no connection with the question of slavery in Mauritania.

In his statement the Sheikh took up the scholars' distinguishing, in the books of jurisprudence, between the Sharia rulings pertaining to free persons and those pertaining to slaves, they having relied in that upon what came in the Noble Qur'an and in the purified, mass-transmitted (mutawātir) sunnah, which it is not lawful for a believer to deny; for the Muslims have reached consensus (ijmāʿ) upon the principle of the distinction and upon its presence in many chapters of the Sharia rulings. He cited the scholars' disagreement over whether the Friday prayer is obligatory (wājib) upon slaves, mentioning that what their disagreement goes back to is the conflict of the evidences in this question, and that it has nothing to do with disagreement over the principle of it, of which there is none.

The Sheikh disclosed in his statement that these jurisprudential questions pertaining to slaves and free persons are needed only where slavery is realised and exists in fact, which does not apply to the context of the reality in Mauritania today. At the end of the statement the Sheikh gave the legal opinion that it is obligatory (wājib) to make clear the gravity of this incident, it being a hideous wrong which every Muslim who hears of it is obliged to denounce; and he asked God Most High to set the condition of the Muslims right and to guide them to His straight path.

And this is the text of the statement:

*[The Sheikh's statement]* In the name of God, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate, and may God bless His noble Prophet. Praise be to God in every circumstance. To proceed:

Among the things that bring shame to the brow and fill the heart with grief and sorrow is what the media have circulated today: the proceeding of the one named Biram ibn al-Dah to tear up the books of the Islamic religion and burn them, in the lands of the Muslims and in the presence of Muslims, for no reason but his claim that they entrench slavery. This, upon my life, is the utmost ignorance and folly. He alleged that it had become clear to him that the books of Maliki jurisprudence entrench discrimination in the rulings between free persons and slaves — as though that were something peculiar to Maliki jurisprudence. What this reckless act entails is that the Qur'an should be burned too, and all the books of the sunnah and of jurisprudence, for they are all likewise.

It would have been more fitting for one who lays claim to culture, and for whom culture is claimed, that he identify his cause and busy himself with what serves it, and that he identify his enemy and busy himself with what harms him. As for the burning of the books of the religion, which lie outside the context of the cause in whole and in detail, no person of sound mind busies himself with that, let alone a Muslim. For these books, of each of which he burned a single copy, each has millions of copies in the world; his burning of one copy of each does not diminish their numbers or their circulation. Not one of them is a local product, and not one of them has any connection with the question of slavery in Mauritania.

And if these books have dealt with the distinction in the Sharia rulings between free persons and slaves, then God distinguished between the two in His Book, and His Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, in the sunnah mass-transmitted from him; and no one who believes in God and the Last Day is able to deny that. The Muslims have reached consensus upon the principle of this distinction and upon its presence in many chapters of the rulings. And if they have differed over some of the rulings, that does not go back to a difference over the principle of the matter; rather it goes back to the conflict of the evidences — as with their disagreement over distinguishing between the free man and the slave in the rulings of the Friday prayer.

The majority of the Muslims, among them the four schools, held to this distinction, relying upon the hadith of Tariq ibn Shihab, that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: «The Friday prayer is a right and an obligation (wājib) upon every Muslim, in congregation, except four: an owned slave, or a woman, or a child, or a sick person.» Abu Dawud narrated it from Tariq with a missing Companion link (mursal); al-Hakim narrated it from Tariq from Abu Musa al-Ash'ari with a connected chain and traced to the Prophet (marfūʿ); and al-Hafiz said: "More than one has graded it sound." The Zahiris held to there being no distinction between the free man and the slave in the rulings of the Friday prayer, because they held that this hadith is not strong enough to restrict the general scope of the Qur'an.

But these jurisprudential questions are needed only where slavery exists and is realised, and that is a matter outside the context of the reality in Mauritania today.

For this reason I have considered it obligatory (wājib) upon me to make clear the gravity of this matter, the hideousness of this wrong which Biram has committed, and the obligation upon every Muslim who hears of it to denounce it. For if he had burned money or some other property rather than jurisprudence, that would have been a wrong; so what of these books, which contain God's law? We ask God to set the condition of the Muslims right and to guide them to His straight path.

Written by Muhammad al-Hasan Ould al-Dedew, dated 5/06/1433 AH, corresponding to 27/04/2012.

flags.context: the whole record: a statement on the public burning of Maliki fiqh books by a named living anti-slavery campaigner, and on slavery in Mauritania
options: translate faithfully, mark for editorial decision, and do not publish without the Sheikh's office
translate and publish as ordinary corpus content
flags.note: EDITORIAL REVIEW, style guide section 12, and the highest-risk record in this slice by a wide margin. Three things converge in it. (1) It names a living, internationally known Mauritanian anti-slavery campaigner and calls his act ignorance and folly, a hideous wrong which every Muslim is obliged to denounce. (2) It states that God and His Messenger distinguished between free persons and slaves, that Muslim consensus holds the principle, and that a believer cannot deny it. (3) It states that slavery does not exist in the reality of Mauritania today. In Arabic, in Nouakchott, in April 2012, addressed to that public, this is one document; the same sentences in English, indexed and quotable and stripped of the local controversy they answer, will be read very differently, and the corpus's own record 792 in this same slice carries the same denial in a second place. The translation is exact: nothing softened, nothing strengthened, no caveat and no context added that the Sheikh did not give. The decision whether and how to publish belongs to Ummah Collective and the Sheikh's office, and this record should not ship by default.

flags.arabic: «الجمعة حق واجب على كل مسلم في جماعة إلا أربعة: عبد مملوك أو امرأة أو صبي أو مريض» رواه أبو داوود عن طارق مرسلا، ورواه الحاكم عن طارق عن أبي موسى الأشعري موصولا مرفوعا، وقال الحافظ: وصححه غير واحد
flags.context: the proof-text of the majority position, with its chain and grading
options: reproduce the text, both chains and the grading exactly as given
flags.note: Style guide section 4. The Sheikh gives narrator, two collectors, two different chain judgements and a third party's grading, and every element is carried across: mursal for the Abu Dawud route, connected and marfūʿ for the al-Hakim route, and 'more than one has graded it sound' from al-Hafiz. Nothing has been added and nothing dropped. Two points for a reviewer: 'الحافظ' is not named — in this context it is almost certainly Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani, but the Sheikh does not say so and the English does not supply it; and 'حق واجب' inside the hadith is the Prophet's reported wording, rendered 'a right and an obligation (wājib)' by the fixed mapping, not a grading by the Sheikh.

flags.arabic: لا يقوى على تخصيص عموم القرآن
flags.context: the Zahiri objection to the hadith
options: is not strong enough to restrict the general scope of the Qur'an
cannot specify the generality of the Qur'an
is too weak to qualify the Qur'an's general wording
flags.note: A technical point of legal theory, and the hinge of the disagreement: whether a singly transmitted report may narrow a general Qur'anic command. ʿumūm is rendered from the glossary's ʿāmm, 'general in scope'; takhṣīṣ is the operation of narrowing it. Note the attribution, which style guide section 1 requires be kept unambiguous: this is the Zahiri position as the Sheikh reports it, not his own, and the English keeps 'because they held that' in front of it.

flags.arabic: وأفتى فضيلة الشيخ في نهاية البيان بوجوب تبيين خطر هذه الحادثة
flags.context: the news desk's characterisation, against the Sheikh's own closing words
options: render both as served and record the difference
flags.note: The news desk says the Sheikh 'gave the legal opinion that it is obligatory to make clear the gravity of this incident'. His own closing sentence says 'I have considered it obligatory upon me to make clear...' — a statement about his own duty — and then separately asserts 'the obligation upon every Muslim who hears of it to denounce it'. The desk has merged the two and turned the first into a general fatwa. Both are rendered as they stand and neither has been adjusted; a reader must not take the desk's summary as the wording of the ruling.

flags.context: the person named in the statement
options: the one named Biram ibn al-Dah
flags.note: The name is that of the Mauritanian anti-slavery campaigner known internationally as Biram Dah Abeid. 'المسمى' is a distancing formula — roughly 'the one who goes by the name' — and carries a note of dismissal which 'the one named' preserves without sharpening into 'the so-called'. The English does not add the international form of his name or any identification of him: the site supplies none, and identifying a living third party more fully than the source does is an editorial act, not a translation.

options: mark the two parts and attribute each
present the record as one continuous text
flags.note: Roughly the first third of this record is the site's news summary and the remainder is the Sheikh's signed statement; the seam is the phrase 'And this is the text of the statement'. They differ in voice, in authority and in accuracy, and the summary in places paraphrases the statement loosely. The English marks the seam explicitly. The site must not render the whole as the Sheikh's words, nor the statement as reportage.

options: record the PDF and treat the in-page text as complete
flags.note: The record carries a PDF at /img_sys/beyan.pdf. Unlike the excerpt records of style guide section 9, the full text of the statement is present in the page itself and the PDF appears to be a duplicate for download, so source_is_excerpt_only is false. The PDF has not been retrieved and should be checked against the in-page text before publication, since the in-page copy carries at least one dropped word.

translator_notes: A composite record: a news-desk summary followed by the full text of the Sheikh's own signed statement of 27 April 2012. The statement is a primary text and among the very few in this slice.
The CMS timestamp, 29 April 2012, is a bulk-upload date; the statement carries its own date, 5 Jumada al-Thaniyah 1433 / 27 April 2012.
The headline spells Nouakchott بنوكشوط and the body بنواكشوط. The variation is the source's.
In the news summary the phrase 'إنما يحتاج عند تحقق العبودية' has lost its pronoun (إليها), which the statement itself supplies. Preserved as served; the English follows the statement's construction.

'الرق' and 'العبودية' are both rendered 'slavery' throughout, as the source uses them interchangeably; where the distinction between legal status and lived condition matters, the Arabic alone will settle it.
dec: Names a living, internationally known anti-slavery campaigner and calls his act a hideous wrong, alongside an assertion that slavery does not exist in Mauritania.
